phase_0.boundary_condition: The fixed integer N and the deterministic arithmetic laws governing its divisors

⊢.justification: The search space begins at the smallest prime, an empty state of no factors yet discovered

⊣.justification: The complete set of prime factors forms the closed boundary containing the entire decomposition

≻.justification: Incrementing the trial divisor moves the search forward through the integer lattice

≺.justification: Dividing N by a found factor reduces the problem size, descending toward the trivial unit

⋈.justification: Chaining successive divisions accumulates the list of discovered prime factors

⊙.justification: A discovered factor is a self-evident truth, an identity that holds within the factorization

∈.justification: The trial division branches into two mutually exclusive paths: divisibility or non-divisibility

∋.justification: The search state reconstitutes after the branch resolves, either with a reduced residue or an incremented divisor

⊤.justification: The remainder is zero, affirming the candidate is a true factor

⊥.justification: The remainder is non-zero, refuting the candidate as a factor

⊞.justification: The state where N is simultaneously composite (has factors) and prime (no factors found yet) during the search process

⊡.justification: Recording a discovered factor into the immutable list of results

phase_2.fuse_result: updated search state (reduced N or incremented d)
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: No divisor tested, N remains untouched
phase_3.true_description: A divisor d is found such that N mod d = 0
phase_3.false_description: A divisor d is tested and N mod d != 0
phase_3.both_description: The search state holds the tension of N being potentially composite while no factor has yet been confirmed

steps.domain_action: Initialize the search with the smallest prime candidate 2
Branch on whether the current candidate divides N
Check if remainder is zero (divisibility confirmed)
Advance the candidate to the next prime if not divisible
Confirm remainder is non-zero (divisibility refuted)
Reduce N by dividing out the found factor
Record the found prime factor in the immutable list
Chain the current factor with the previous list of factors
Verify the factor is self-consistent within the product
Rejoin the search state with the updated residue and candidate
Branch on whether the reduced residue is 1 (complete) or >1 (continue)
Affirm the residue is 1, factorization complete
Refute the residue is 1, more factors exist
Continue the search with the next candidate
Further reduce the residue if a new factor is found
Append the new factor to the record
Update the cumulative product of factors
Self-reference the current state of the factorization
Rejoin the completion check with the continuation path
Hold the state where the number is both fully factored and still being searched
Close the system when the residue reaches 1, containing all factors
Finalize the complete list of prime factors as a permanent record

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The arithmetic rules of integer division and primality testing
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The remainder value passed between the trial division and the reduction step
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The list of discovered prime factors stored in the IFIX register
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The deterministic order of trial divisors from smallest to largest
phase_5.alfs_store: The fundamental theorem of arithmetic guaranteeing a unique factorization

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational cycles for division and modulo operations
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A large composite integer N with unknown factorization
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A list of prime factors whose product equals N
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information content of N is conserved in the list of factors; no information is lost, only reorganized.
